comparison_basis.effort_definition: Git additions/deletions and changed files from each prior layer
comparison_basis.equivalent_evidence_scenario: three tenant-bound cited records correlated in process with stable timeline ordering, shared-fact links, no network, and no causal claim
comparison_basis.equivalent_gateway_scenario: tenant-scoped structured fake-provider call with explicit catalog, pre-call reservation, deterministic route, normalized usage/cost settlement, no network, and no production effect
comparison_basis.equivalent_orchestration_scenario: fixed-role checkout specialist fan-out/fan-in through critic, proposal-only planner and verification-plan gate using deterministic models, in-memory application facts, no network or production effect
comparison_basis.equivalent_remediation_scenario: high-risk checkout Kubernetes rollout-restart with exact immutable plan/action/target/policy digests, two distinct human approvals, dry-run, stable idempotency, deterministic fake effect and fresh verification; in-memory, no network or production credentials

custom_comparison.layer6_tradeoff: HTTPX, PyYAML, and the official Kubernetes client remove transport, syntax, and Kubernetes object decoding only. They do not remove tenant, provenance, SSRF, pagination, ledger, or quarantine controls
custom_comparison.layer7_tradeoff: LangGraph removes custom DAG scheduler, synchronized fan-in, reducers and checkpoint traversal, but application role policy, artifact transitions, fencing, facts, RLS, citations and final gates remain
custom_comparison.layer8_tradeoff: Custom Layer 8 implements its own asynchronous remediation lifecycle over PostgreSQL and Redis delivery. Framework Layer 7 delegates durable waits, timers, signals, Activity retry/heartbeat/cancellation and replay to Temporal, but retains nearly all approval/effect security controls
custom_comparison.runtime_comparison_status: Equivalent network-free fake gateway scenarios ran on the same machine; figures are local implementation latency, not provider or distributed throughput
custom_comparison.temporal_tradeoff: Temporal removes scheduler, timers, signal history, retry/backoff, and crash recovery code but adds a second operational control plane

equivalent_evidence_benchmark.limitations: Different Pydantic/dataclass contracts; excludes PostgreSQL, Temporal, Redis, connector networks, ingestion, and process boundaries

equivalent_gateway_benchmark.limitations: Different internal sync/async APIs; no PostgreSQL, Temporal, Redis, provider network, serialization, or process boundary was included

equivalent_orchestration_benchmark.limitations: Both use deterministic in-memory fixtures, but custom includes its async event repository and creates an event loop per sample while framework includes strict Pydantic artifacts and LangGraph checkpoints; no PostgreSQL, Temporal, Redis, network or process boundary is included

equivalent_remediation_benchmark.limitations: Both execute deterministic in-memory high-risk approval/effect paths. Custom is async and includes its event repository/lease machinery; framework is sync and includes strict Pydantic contracts/pure ledger. Neither benchmark includes PostgreSQL, Temporal, Redis, Kubernetes, network, serialization or process boundaries
